title: Commanders Pro Bowl LT Laremy Tunsil out indefinitely after tearing triceps in training camp
description: One of the top left tackles in the NFL is going to miss a lot of time.
fullText:
One of the top left tackles in the NFL won't be playing for a while.

Washington Commanders Pro Bowler Laremy Tunsil tore his triceps during training camp on Saturday and will likely require surgery, causing him to miss at least a significant portion of the regular season according to NFL Network's Mike Garafalo.

Tunsil reportedly sustained the injury in a 1-on-1 drill while taking on a bull rush from Odafe Oweh, who joined the Commanders on a four-year, $100 million contract in free agency this offseason.

The Commanders also paid up with Tunsil this offseason, signing him to a two-year, $60.2 million contract extension in March that made him the highest paid offensive tackle in the NFL by average annual value.

Tunsil is entering his second season with the Commanders after joining them last summer via a blockbuster trade with the Houston Texans. Pro Football Focus ranked him as the third-best pass blocker at the position in his first season.

The Commanders are now left to figure out how they will protect star quarterback Jayden Daniels in 2026. ESPN's Adam Schefter quickly pointed to veteran Andrew Wylie as the next man up at left tackle while Josh Conerly Jr. remains at right tackle. Brandon Coleman, the Commanders' former starter at LT, also got starts there when Tunsil was injured last season, but has been making the transition to guard.

Washington has a little more than a month to figure that out, with their season-opener scheduled for Sept. 13 against the Philadelphia Eagles.

title: NFL Personality Rips ‘Soft as Brie Cheese’ Packers in NFC North Verdict
description: The Green Bay Packers are trying to move past a collapse that ended a promising 2025 season.Colin Cowherd already sees a problem that could follow them into 2026.Cowherd took aim at head coach Matt LaFleur and Green Bay’s toughness during the Aug. 7 edition of “The Herd,” questioning whether the Packers have enough edge to […] The post NFL Personality Rips ‘Soft as Brie Cheese’ Packers in NFC North Verdict appeared first on HEAVY.
fullText:
The Green Bay Packers are trying to move past a collapse that ended a promising 2025 season.

Colin Cowherd already sees a problem that could follow them into 2026.

Cowherd took aim at head coach Matt LaFleur and Green Bay's toughness during the Aug. 7 edition of "The Herd," questioning whether the Packers have enough edge to survive a loaded NFC North.

"Soft as brie cheese in a town that loves aged cheddar," via The Herd's segment shared on X.

The post added that Cowherd believes LaFleur and the Packers "aren't tough enough to win big" in the division.

"Soft as brie cheese in a town that loves aged cheddar."@colincowherd argues Matt LaFleur & the Packers aren't tough enough to win big in the stacked NFC North pic.twitter.com/StvkwsH4np

— Herd w/Colin Cowherd (@TheHerd) August 7, 2026

It's pointed reproval for a coach who has won plenty of regular-season games in Green Bay.

LaFleur enters his eighth season with a 76-40-1 record, six playoff appearances and a new multiyear contract.

The question surrounding him has gone toward the up-in-the-air direction.

The Packers know LaFleur can get them into January. But Cowherd and others question whether his teams have the edge to finish once they get there.

GettyGREEN BAY, WISCONSIN – DECEMBER 07: Head coach Matt Lafleur of the Green Bay Packers reacts to a unsportsmanlike conduct penalty during the second quarter against the Chicago Bears at Lambeau Field on December 07, 2025 in Green Bay, Wisconsin. (Photo by John Fisher/Getty Images)

Green Bay gave Cowherd plenty of material during the final weeks of 2025.

The Packers were 9-3-1 before losing their final four regular-season games. Their season ended with a 31-27 wild-card loss to the Chicago Bears after Green Bay led 21-3 at halftime and 27-16 in the fourth quarter.

Jordan Love threw for 323 yards and four touchdowns in the loss, but the offense went through four third-quarter possessions while picking up only one first down.

The late-game problems went past one night.

NFL.com noted when LaFleur signed his extension that the Packers became the first team since the 1970 merger to lose three games in one season, including the playoffs, after holding a lead of at least 10 points in the final five minutes.

Two of those losses came against Chicago.

Injuries deserve a place in the discussion.

Micah Parsons suffered a torn ACL in Week 15, and Green Bay dealt with other significant absences down the stretch.

Still, the way games slipped away can't out of view.

Packers president Ed Policy did not see it as a reason to move on from LaFleur. Green Bay signed LaFleur, general manager Brian Gutekunst and executive vice president/director of football operations Russ Ball to multiyear extensions in January.

GettyLOS ANGELES, CALIFORNIA – FEBRUARY 09: Colin Cowherd attends the The Volume Anniversary Party on February 09, 2022 in Los Angeles, California. (Photo by Jerod Harris/Getty Images for The Volume )

Cowherd's denunciation also has history behind it.

He made a similar argument in November 2022, saying the Packers had become "softer" under LaFleur and questioning the team's identity after a loss to Philadelphia.

Up to today, the quarterback has changed and much of the roster has turned over.

But Cowherd is harping on the same issue.

There is also a difference between LaFleur being under pressure and being on the hot seat.

Green Bay gave him a legitimate multiyear commitment less than seven months ago.

Policy said in March that it had "never been clearer" to him that the Packers had the right football leadership in place. He also said he had decided before the playoff game that he wanted LaFleur back.

That puts the focus on what happens on the field.

LaFleur has a 3-6 playoff record, and Green Bay has failed to reach the NFC Championship Game since the 2020 season.

The Packers have also gone one-and-done in each of the past two postseasons.

Cowherd's cheese line will get the attention, but the actual challenge sits underneath it.

Green Bay has already committed to LaFleur.

At any rate, his team has to show it can close the games that have kept it from becoming a championship team.

Former Pittsburgh Steelers coach Mike Tomlin is one of the most decorated coaches of his era with an NFL stint that has spanned decades. Tomlin became a football analyst after he stepped down as head coach of the Steelers in January of this year. In his 19-year run, he never had a losing season with the team and won Super Bowl XLIII. title: Cardinals rookie QB Carson Beck impresses as he gets first NFL snaps in Hall of Fame Game
description: The NFL got the preseason going on Thursday night with the Hall of Fame Game.
fullText:
At some point this season, the Arizona Cardinals seem likely to get rookie Carson Beck some starts. They gave him one on Thursday to start that process.

And if the rest of the preseason goes as well as Thursday did, the push to get the rookie some regular-season starts might happen earlier than expected.

Beck, a third-round pick who was a college star at Georgia and Miami, started for the Cardinals against the Carolina Panthers as the NFL got the preseason started with the Hall of Fame Game in Canton, Ohio. Beck looked good.

He looked quite comfortable as he took the Cardinals on a 96-yard touchdown drive to end the first quarter. The Cardinals were backed up near their own end zone when Beck made a big play. Receiver Jalen Brooks made a nice double move and Beck hit him downfield for a 35-yard gain. Later in the drive he had a nice pass to Brooks over the middle, delivering an accurate throw despite tight coverage for 15 yards. Beck completed a pass to the 1-yard line and then running back Corey Kiner scored the first unofficial touchdown of the NFL season to start the second quarter.

Carson Beck deep shot on third down 🚀

(via @NFL)pic.twitter.com/lwcAR9TDB3

Beck finished the first quarter 8 of 9 for 81 yards. On Beck's first pass of the second quarter, he threw deep to Brooks, who hauled it in for 49 yards. Beck wasn't nervous about pushing the ball downfield, which is a good sign. Then Beck threw a nice fade route for a third-and-goal touchdown to Simi Fehoko.

Carson Beck throws his first career NFL touchdown for the Cardinals 👏

(via @NFL)pic.twitter.com/cVmC2XNNMv

Beck was playing with and against plenty of players who won't make 53-man rosters, but it was still a promising first game. He played one series in the second half before he was replaced, finishing 15 of 19 for 188 yards. Given how it was the only game of the week after a long offseason, there will surely be plenty of overreaction over Beck's strong performance.

The Cardinals have veterans Jacoby Brissett and Gardner Minshew II on the roster. Brissett will likely begin the season as the starter, but Arizona has a tough early schedule, and at some point the team might want to get a look at Beck. If Arizona finishes with one of the NFL's worst records, as it did last season, the Cardinals will want to know what they have in Beck before entering a 2027 NFL Draft that is deep at quarterback.

Arizona is already invested in Beck. Beck was the 65th overall pick, the first selection of the third round — a valuable pick for a Cardinals team that is in the middle of a rebuild. Clearly Arizona wanted to take a shot on Beck, who helped Georgia and then Miami win a lot of games. He was a productive college quarterback but also had UCL surgery on his elbow during his college career. He threw 12 interceptions in each of his last two seasons, and there were reports before the draft that his personality rubbed teams the wrong way. That's why he slid to the third round, though he did lead off the round.

The Cardinals still have three more preseason games and they'll keep getting Beck reps in preseason games. The first look at him on an NFL field was clearly a positive.

title: Fox CEO Lachlan Murdoch says network won’t redo NFL deal until after 2029-30 opt-out
description: Fox Corporation CEO Lachlan Murdoch broke some major news during his company’s quarterly earnings call on Thursday morning. fullText:
Fox Corporation CEO Lachlan Murdoch broke some major news during his company's quarterly earnings call on Thursday morning.

After about a year of speculation that the NFL and its incumbent broadcast partners would engage in talks to renegotiate media rights deals several years prior to the league's opt-out options at the end of the decade, with the upshot being that the NFL would earn more money from its broadcast partners now and, in exchange, remove its opt-out clauses, guaranteeing its partners remain in business with the league well into the 2030s, Fox has decided it will instead roll the dice and reengage with the NFL following the 2029-30 season.

Murdoch told investors that Fox "will not be making any amendments" to its current NFL media rights deal until the league's opt-out option hits following 2029-30. The Fox CEO added that the decision was made as a result of talks with the NFL.

Fox CEO: Decision a result of talks with NFL

— Brian Steinberg (@bristei) August 6, 2026

"We don't see any changes to our contractual terms until the 2030 season," Murdoch told investors later in the call, offering little detail about why or how this decision was made. "Our relationship with the NFL is an incredibly positive one. We engage with them all the time," he continued, adding he sees "a clear path forward" following the league's opt-out.

Fox CEO Lachlan Murdoch said on the company’s Q4 earnings call just now that it won’t look to open up its NFL deal until after the 2029-30 season.

“We don’t see any changes to our contractual terms until the 2030 season.”

— Josh Carpenter (@JoshACarpenter) August 6, 2026

Fox CEO: Will take up rights talks much closer to the end of the contract. 'Very pleased' with recent decision to strike deal for Mexican rights and sees 'a clear path forward' after 2029

— Brian Steinberg (@bristei) August 6, 2026

The comments come as a considerable development in the league's effort to negotiate new terms to its broadcast deals, which the NFL sees as significantly undervalued in the current market for media rights. Fox's decision comes just days after reports surfaced that talks between the NFL and CBS had stalled on account of Paramount's impending merger with Warner Bros. Discovery. Prior to Murdoch's confirmation that Fox's decision was a result of talks it had with the NFL, CBS was the only network to have been confirmed in active discussions with the league over its media rights.

Fox's decision perhaps shouldn't come as much of a surprise. Once the NFL made clear its desires to renegotiate broadcast rights early, angling to increase its annual TV revenue by billions of dollars, Fox launched a covert political pressure campaign reaching the highest levels of federal government, including the president. As a result, numerous arms of the federal government began scrutinizing the NFL's media business. The Department of Justice launched an investigation into potential anticompetitive practices from the NFL. The chairman of the Federal Communications Commission regularly opined on whether the NFL was running afoul of its antitrust exemption, which allows the league to bundle and sell its media rights to broadcasters in packages on behalf of its 32 franchises. Congressional hearings were held on the move of live sports broadcasts from linear television to streaming. Legislation was announced addressing the fragmentation of live sports broadcasts.

Whether any of these efforts had real standing to change how the NFL conducts its media business is unclear. But the onslaught of political pressure, at the very least, created a roadblock for the league that forced its timeline for negotiations to shift back.

Now, the question falls to the NFL's other broadcast partners. CBS will presumably still need to come to new terms with the league prior to the 2029-30 opt-out because of the change-of-control provision triggered in its current contract following Skydance's purchase of Paramount last summer. The NFL, if it chooses, could exit its CBS deal early because of that clause, whereas it is locked in with every other partner through at least the end of the decade.

Fox's decision, however, might convince the NFL's other partners — NBC, ESPN, and Prime Video — to wait until the league's opt-out options hit before renegotiating. At the very least, it would ensure their media rights bills don't increase by potentially billions of dollars in the interim years.

If that is the case, the NFL's efforts to redo its deals early could reasonably be seen as a major failure of the league. However, it opens up a whole host of possibilities for how the league might choose to restructure its broadcast deals a few years from now, when it can break clean and divvy up inventory in whatever way it wants.

fullText:
Company acquired in deal involving Affinity Partners, a firm run by Donald Trump’s son-in-law Jared Kushner

Electronic Arts, the maker of video games such as The Sims, Madden NFL and Battlefield, has been bought by Saudi Arabia’s wealth fund and a group of investors for $55bn (£41bn).

The company announced the completion of the deal on Tuesday evening, only days after the EU gave its approval, the final regulatory green light needed.

EA is best known for its blockbuster sports games including EA Sports FC (previously called Fifa). In what is one of the biggest buyouts on record, EA Games is being taken private, ending its 36-year history as a publicly traded company.

The company has been bought by Saudi Arabia’s PIF along with Affinity Partners, a private equity company run by Donald Trump’s son-in-law Jared Kushner and the private equity firm Silver Lake Partners.

“EA has created stories, characters, and communities that have become part of everyday life for hundreds of millions of people,” Kushner said. “We’re excited to support the company as it continues to reach new audiences, inspire the next generation of creators, and expand the ways people around the world connect through play.”

The Saudi royal family has been investing in video games and esports for some time, alongside sports, media and comedy, while the Saudi crown prince, Mohammed bin Salman, has a reputation for being a gamer.

EA was founded by the former Apple employee William “Trip” Hawkins in 1982. Hawkins began playing analog versions of baseball and football made by Strat-O-Matic as a teenager during the 1960s. The company has been run by its current chief executive, Andrew Wilson, since 2013.

EA’s games still have a dedicated fanbase, although its annual revenues have stagnated in recent years, hovering between $7.4bn and $7.6bn.

Competition from mobile video game makers, such as Epic Games, has intensified in recent years, and one of EA’s biggest rivals, Activision Blizzard, was bought by Microsoft for almost $69bn in 2023.

As a private company, EA will no longer be required to report its financial results each quarter, freeing it from some scrutiny, which some analysts say can remove some pressure to meet targets.

However, there are often job cuts and cost-cutting at formerly public companies when they are taken private, although there has not been any suggestion that this will happen at EA.

The company laid off about 5% of its workforce in 2024 but had 14,500 employees in March 2025 and cut several hundred jobs in May.

On Monday, EA reported lower than expected revenues in the last quarter, blamed on a decline in engagement with its latest Battlefield game.

title: Dan Lanning studying NFL tape to help Oregon overcome rematch curse
description: The Ducks have notoriously struggled in rematches in recent years, and Dan Lanning is looking to the next level to help Oregon get over the hump.
fullText:
The Oregon Ducks have mastered the regular season under Dan Lanning. Since entering the Big Ten, the Ducks have lost just one regular season game, falling at home to Indiana last season in a tight battle.

That puts the Ducks on the path to the postseason routinely, but one reason the program hasn't overcome its demons in the playoffs yet is because of the potential for a rematch.

In 2023, Oregon came up short against Washington twice, including in the Pac-12 Championship game rematch with a spot in the College Football Playoff on the line. The following season, the Ducks took down Ohio State in a thriller at Autzen Stadium, but fell flat in the Rose Bowl to end the season.

Last season was a familiar story. The Ducks played hard against the Hoosiers in Eugene, but fell apart from the first snap of the Peach Bowl in another blowout loss to end the season. So, how do the Ducks do something different to hurdle the last obstacle in their path to a championship?

Lanning has spent the offseason working to find a solution, and he's turned to the NFL for answers.

"It's most common in the NFL," Lanning told reporters on Monday. "You know, so just more so conversations with approach and what that might look like. You know, it's a little bit different. I won't hop into great detail on it, but there's certainly some things that I think we've learned from and can use."

On paper, it makes sense. The NFL schedule requires teams to play the other three teams in their division twice. More often than not, teams that make the playoffs will play some teams for a second or even a third time. Rematches are commonplace, and the best teams know how to win them to advance.

The reigning Super Bowl champions, the Seattle Seahawks, are a perfect example. The Seahawks had to play a pair of division rivals three times. The San Francisco 49ers and Los Angeles Rams beat the Seahawks in their first meeting, but the Seahawks won the final two games against both, including wins in the playoffs over both teams, en route to a championship.

That's the goal for Lanning and the Ducks in 2026. Even if Oregon stumbles in an early matchup, the Ducks need to have better answers and a better mentality going into a rematch.

"Coach Lanning does a great job just finding keys and details of certain things that will help us as a team," Oregon quarterback Dante Moore said. "I wasn't a part of that with him, what he was doing, but it's just true. You just got to find things from different teams. You know, you never want to be too big-headed. You always want to learn from somebody."

Where could that rematch come from? The Ducks will play several playoff contenders in conference play, including USC, Michigan and Ohio State. The Ducks and Buckeyes are two of the top contenders to win it all, and they could have a rematch in the Big Ten championship game or in the playoffs, depending on how the season shakes out.

Moore knows he needs to be sharper in bigger games, and he said he's treating last season's games against Indiana as lessons rather than losses. But he's also trusting his supporting cast and coaches to put the Ducks in a position to succeed.

"You know, Indiana, for example, did a great job last year on Ohio State," Moore said. "Everybody copied that defense. So it's going to be a lot of things that happen with change. That's how football works. But yeah, I know coach Lanning. I'm trusting his game plan, and I'm excited for this year."

title: Garett Bolles’ 2025 All-Pro season vaults him up this year’s NFL Top 100 list
description: Former Ute All-American offensive tackle makes second appearance on prestigious list voted on by peers.
fullText:
Garett Bolles’ best season as a pro led to another honor, this time from his peers.

The Utah native and Denver Broncos left tackle came in at No. 42 in this year’s NFL Top 100 rankings, a list compiled by the league each offseason and voted on by NFL players.

This is the 16th year of the rankings, and for Bolles, it’s the highest he’s ever been ranked.

No. 42 on the NFL Top 100 Players of 2026…@broncos OT Garett Bolles! @NFLFilms pic.twitter.com/V0HcCsuTKN

Bolles earned first-team All-Pro honors during the 2025 season, after he didn’t allow a sack in 1,126 snaps played. He was also named to the Pro Bowl for the first time in his career.

During his ninth NFL season, Bolles earned an 89.3 overall Pro Football Focus grade while allowing a pressure rate of 5.9%, which was the lowest at his position last season and the second-lowest among left tackles since 2018, per the NFL.

It was the second-straight year Bolles had the lowest pressure rate at his position, with a 4.5% in 2024.

This is the second time Bolles, who prepped at Westlake High in Utah, and also played at Snow College before becoming an All-American at the University of Utah, has appeared on the NFL Top 100 rankings.

In 2021, he made his first appearance on the list at No. 82 after earning second-team All-Pro honors the previous season.

“I don’t respect a lot of tackles, I’ll tell you that. Garett is a guy I respect,” Giants linebacker Kayvon Thibodeaux said of Bolles in a video shared on social media announcing him at the No. 42 spot.

“He plays all four quarters. That’s something that it’s tough to do, especially at that offensive tackle position, especially when you got edge guys like we do in this league. He’s one of those dudes that are just hard to get around.”

The 2026 version of the NFL Top 100 rankings will continue to be released through Sept. 4. Each day, the league releases two more players on the list — on Monday, that includes players ranked No. 40 and No. 39, and once it reaches the top 10, the NFL will announce one spot at a time.

Entering the 2026 NFL season, the Green Bay Packers and star quarterback Jordan Love are facing an immense amount of pressure.

Over the last couple of years, the Packers have had Super Bowl expectations. Unfortunately, they have come up short of those expectations come playoff time.

Last offseason, the team went all-in on pursuing a championship. The trade for superstar pass rusher Micah Parsons was supposed to be the final piece of the puzzle. Due to injuries and a Wild Card collapse against the Chicago Bears, Green Bay ended the year in disappointment.

Heading into the 2026 season, Love and the Packers are once again viewed as a potential Super Bowl caliber team. For them to reach that level of hype, they’re going to need Love to take the next step.

With that being said, Love spoke out with a clear warning to the rest of the NFL early on during training camp.

While there are many who question the supporting cast Green Bay has put around Love, the quarterback himself is expecting big things from the offense.

If the offensive line can step up and keep Love upright and healthy, Green Bay does appear to have the makings of a special offense. But, it will be up to Love to make sure that expectation becomes a reality.

Since taking over as the Packers’ starting quarterback following Aaron Rodgers’ departure, Love has been very good. However, he has come up just short of being great.

Last season, the 27-year-old signal caller played in 15 games. He completed 66.3 percent of his pass attempts for 3,381 yards, 23 touchdowns, and six interceptions. Outside of the completion percentage, those numbers were slightly lower than 2024.

During that 2024 season, Love threw for 3,389 yards, 25 touchdowns, and 11 interceptions in 15 games. He threw for 4,159 yards, 32 touchdowns, and 11 interceptions in 2023.

There is no denying that Love has legitimate superstar potential. However, it’s time for him to actually turn that potential into production on the field in 2026.

title: Cowboys Waive 6-foot-6, 250-Pound Edge Rusher Facing 3-Game Suspension
description: The Dallas Cowboys have waived free-agent edge rusher Charles Snowden, who is facing a 3-game suspension from the NFL. The post Cowboys Waive 6-foot-6, 250-Pound Edge Rusher Facing 3-Game Suspension appeared first on HEAVY.
fullText:
The Dallas Cowboys were willing to take a chance on edge rusher Charles Snowden — they just weren’t willing to wait for him to heal up as they try to improve the NFL’s worst defense from 1 season ago.

“The Cowboys have signed OL Sebastian Gutierrez and waived OLB Charles Snowden,” The Athletic’s Jon Machota wrote on his official X account on Sunday.

Snowden signed a 1-year, $1.075 million contract with the Cowboys on June 18 and was suspended almost 1 month later. Snowden was waived with an injury designation as he was dealing with a groin issue.

“Cowboys DE Charles Snowden has been suspended for the first three games of the season, per today’s wire,” ESPN’s Adam Schefter wrote on his official X account on July 14. “Snowden, per the NFL, ‘is eligible to participate in all preseason activities, including games; his suspension will take effect as of the roster reduction to 53 players.”

He was arrested for a DUI in Las Vegas in December 2024 and pleaded no contest in January 2026.

“Cowboys DE Charles Snowden has been suspended for the first three games of the season because of a DUI,” NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport wrote on his official X account on July 14. “The news of his personal conduct violation was on today’s wire.”

Snowden would have been eligible to return to the Cowboys for a Week 4 home game against the Arizona Cardinals.

Snowden, 6-foot-6 and 250 pounds, started 9 games each of the last 2 seasons for the Las Vegas Raiders, with 67 tackles, 4.5 sacks, 8 TFL, and 11 QB hits in that stretch.

NFL draft analyst Lance Zierlein projected Snowden as a 4th-round pick in 2021.

“Versatile defender who has worked both open and closed sides as an even-front edge defender,” Zierlein wrote. “Snowden is a long, smooth athlete dropping into space or transitioning with change of direction. Lower-body anchor is an issue and he needs more play strength, but he’s usually first to land his hands and does an adequate job of separating and setting the edge. Despite having some twitch with his get-off as a rusher, he gets locked out of the cookie jar due to an inability to convert at the top of the rush with hand usage or go-to counters. However, he has excellent lateral quickness for use in twists and stunts and has surprising potential as a zone or man defender when asked. Snowden is an ascending prospect with Day 2 potential as a 3-4 outside linebacker, but his ceiling will be defined by whether he can add mass and improve his rush.”

After going undrafted out of the University of Virginia, Snowden made the Chicago Bears as an undrafted free agent in 2021 and spent 2022 on the practice squad for the Tampa Bay Buccaneers before landing with the Raiders in 2023.

“Sources: The Cowboys are signing former Raiders DE Charles Snowden.” NFL Insider Jordan Schultz posted on X on June 18. “Over the last two seasons, Snowden started 18 games for Las Vegas — recording 4.5 sacks and 8 tackles for loss.”

Snowden is part of a group of new Cowboys being brought in to revitalize the edge rusher position after a complete miss in 2025 — a year that began with NFL All-Pro Micah Parsons being traded to the Green Bay Packers.

Along with signing Snowden, the Cowboys made 2 more notable moves at edge rusher. First, they traded with the Packers for former 1st-round pick Rashan Gary.

Second, they used the 2nd of their 2 picks in the 1st round of the draft on UCF’s Malachi Lawrence at No. 23 overall.

title: Giants' game-by-game predictions for 2026 season in first year under John Harbaugh
description: Predicting how the New York Giants will fare in the 2026 NFL season.
fullText:
Giants' game-by-game predictions for 2026 season in first year under John Harbaugh originally appeared on The Sporting News. Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here.

The New York Giants are a team on the rise in the eyes of many. Things began to transform for the team last season when Jaxson Dart was inserted as the team's starting quarterback and the hiring of John Harbaugh as the team's new head coach this offseason was a sign that this organization means business.

The Giants have made the playoffs just once in the last decade and the team is 13-38 across the last three seasons. It was time for a culture change and if anyone can implement that in a positive way, it's Harbaugh, the long-time coach of the Baltimore Ravens.

The Giants will be a trendy dark-horse pick this season in a league where teams routinely go from worst to first in their divisions. The Philadelphia Eagles have won the division in each of the last two seasons, becoming the first team to win the division in back-to-back years since they did it back in 2003 and 2024.

Week 1: September 13 vs. Dallas Cowboys

What a way to open the season. The Giants will host the Cowboys on Sunday Night Football and this will be a great chance to start the Harbaugh era out with a bang. The Cowboys are going to get a trendy NFC pick to compete this season as well, so they will be up for this one.

A healthy Giants team with Dart, Malik Nabers and Cam Skattebo get the Harbaugh era off to a good start with the game being played at MetLife Stadium being the key factor.

Week 2: September 21 at Los Angeles Rams

The Giants go from a Sunday night game to a Monday night game. The Rams are going to be one of the best teams in the league this season and this young Giants team won't be ready for this kind of challenge just yet.

Week 3: September 27 vs. Tennessee Titans

The Giants have their first game that isn't on primetime television and against a Titans team that is still looking to create an identity with new head coach Robert Saleh. This game will be more competitive than some might expect but the Giants get out with the win.

Week 4: October 4 vs. Arizona Cardinals

This is where getting to play that last-place schedule can get teams off to a good start. The Cardinals appear to be one of the weaker teams in the league in 2026 with their new head coach Mike LaFleur and it's another game where the Giants get to play at home. That will be one of the biggest factors in the first quadrant of this season's schedule.

Week 5: October 11 at Washington Commanders

This is definitely a winnable game for the Giants, but the Commanders are a solid opponent with Jayden Daniels at quarterback, particularly on the road. It could go either way but the Commanders kick a game-winning field goal with just seconds left to take the first matchup between the teams this season.

Week 6: October 11 vs. New Orleans Saints

The Saints are a team, like the Giants, that many expect to be much better this season. But this is a game where the Giants' defense uses the noise of the home crowd to its advantage and forces the young quarterback Tyler Shough into a couple of mistakes that swing the result in their favor.

Week 7: October 25 at Houston Texans

This could be one of the biggest tests Dart faces this year as the Texans have arguably the best defense in the NFL. This one could be one of those 60-minute dogfights where in the end, the Texans' defense just makes it too difficult for the Giants to score many points.

Week 9: November 8 at Philadelphia Eagles

This is going to be one of the best games of the season. The Giants will be coming off their bye week and though they have to travel to Philly, this will be the third divisional matchup in a row for the Eagles, which comes right before their bye week.

They're going to be ready for a break and the Giants will be able to take advantage of that to steal one on the road.

Week 10: November 12 vs. Washington Commanders

It's a short week coming off a hard-fought win over the Eagles, but it's a home game. The Giants get one back on the Commanders here after an earlier loss.

Week 11: November 22 vs. Jacksonville Jaguars

The nice thing about playing on a Thursday night is having 10 days to rest before the next game. The Giants will then play host to the Jaguars, who were terrific last season, but several analysts believe they will take a step back this season after what many feel was a rough offseason for the team.

This game between inter-conference opponents feels like it has the makings for a shootout.

Week 12: November 29 at Indianapolis Colts

This will be the Giants' last game against the AFC South this season, and it will be one that Colts quarterback Daniel Jones has circled on his calendar. This will be his chance for some revenge against the team that drafted him and then later released him. Will he be healthy at that stage of the season?

If he is, he gets that measure of revenge against his former squad.

Week 13: December 6 vs. San Francisco 49ers

Any time you play the 49ers, the immediate question surrounds the health of their team. Kyle Shanahan seems to deal with more injuries than any coach in the league by a lot, but he always has his team disciplined and ready to play regardless. The Giants will take a loss in this game but it will be one of those defeats where they learn quite a bit about where they stand the rest of the way.

Week 14: December 3 at Seattle Seahawks

This has turned into a tough stretch in the schedule for the G-Men. A trip to Lumen Field to face the defending champions doesn't help.

Week 15: December 20 vs. Cleveland Browns

What was becoming such a promising season for the Giants has drastically turned following a three-game losing streak, but this matchup is just what the doctor ordered.

Whether it's Deshaun Watson, Shedeur Sanders, or someone else at quarterback for the Browns, this is a game where the trio of Brian Burns, Abdul Carter and Kayvon Thibodeaux takes over. The Giants register eight sacks in this game as they pound the Browns, a team Harbaugh knows a lot about beating.

Week 16: December 28 at Detroit Lions

The Giants get their second game of the season on Monday Night Football and it could easily be a playoff-like atmosphere in the Motor City. The Lions will be hungry for a win here and the Giants will find out again that they are just a notch below some of the top-flight NFC teams.

Week 17: January 3 at Dallas Cowboys

Just after the New Year, it's a Week 1 rematch in a game where playoff positioning at this stage of the season will be very important. The health of these two teams and whether or not there is anything to play for will make a big difference in this one, but assuming playoff spots could be on the line for both teams, the Giants come up short of the season sweep over the Cowboys.

Week 18: Date/Time TBD vs. Philadelphia Eagles

The Giants get to finish the season at home and have a chance to sweep the Eagles, something they have not done since 2007. Whether or not nine wins gets the Giants into the playoffs would be questionable, but they play spirited ball in this game to show that not only was Harbaugh the right choice as the team's head coach, but that the future is incredibly bright.

title: NFL insider shares stellar reviews of Myles Garrett, Trent McDuffie from camp
description: Albert Breer says Myles Garrett has been "better than advertised" and the Rams believe Trent McDuffie can be the best DB in football.
fullText:
There’s been a lot of hype surrounding Myles Garrett and Trent McDuffie as the Los Angeles Rams’ blockbuster additions this offseason. Garrett is the reigning Defensive Player of the Year and McDuffie is a two-time All-Pro, each making the Rams defense significantly better.

As exciting as those two newcomers are, it appears they’ve been even better than anticipated. Albert Breer of Sports Illustrated visited Rams training camp recently and he says Garrett has been better than advertised, fitting “in seamlessly.”

As for McDuffie, Breer wouldn’t be surprised if he’s a captain in his first season with the Rams, and that the team thinks he “can become perhaps the NFL’s best defensive back” in a similar role to what Jalen Ramsey played in L.A.

The buzz about the new guys is very real. Myles Garrett has been, believe it or not, better than advertised, has fit in seamlessly and should benefit from having a deep, loaded group of defensive linemen around him. And Trent McDuffie has checked every box, as a guy who can play field, boundary and slot corner, and is a tough, physical tone-setter—I wouldn’t be surprised if he’s a captain in his first year as a Ram. The team believes he can become perhaps the NFL’s best defensive back in a role not unlike the one that Jalen Ramsey (who, admittedly, is a bigger, more physically imposing player) played in Los Angeles. Those two guys alone should make a very significant difference, and that’s with all due respect to Jared Verse, who was part of the cost of getting Garrett.

The Rams were thrilled to acquire both players this offseason and it's easy to see why. Garrett is the unanimous best edge rusher in the NFL, and McDuffie is a premier cornerback – both in the slot and on the outside.

If they live up to expectations, Los Angeles' defense is going to be a terrifying unit.

title: See the Burnley FC kit J.J. Watt designed and promoted as 'The Milkman'
description: J.J. Watt tapped into his "Milk Man" persona to promote Burnley FC's away kit that he designed. The former NFL star is a minority owner in the club.
fullText:
The cream always rises to the top.

That's the message J.J. Watt is injecting into Burnley FC, the English soccer club that he is a minority investor in.

The former Houston Texans great tapped into his "Milk Man" persona to help design the side's cream-colored away kit for the 2026-2027 season. Burnley, which was founded in 1882, released a lighthearted promotional video called "The Cream Rises" on Friday, July 31 to share the design with the world.

In in the visual, Watt plays a local milk man. After starting his day among cows and sheep, he drives a milk float through the countryside, dropping off deliveries to local legends, including cricket great Sir Jimmy Anderson and entrepreneur Dave Fishwick. Instead of actual cream, the goods delivered are one of the new kits. The defensive star ends his trip at Turf Moor, the Clarets' stadium, showing off the full Castore jersey with the cream base and horizontal red and green stripes.

"From day one, I didn't want this to be just another football shirt. I wanted to create something quintessentially Burnley," Watt said in a statement on the team's website. "Every decision we made started with one question: are we doing the supporters of this club proud? As I’ve said many times before, this club existed long before I arrived and it will exist long after I’m gone. But during this time, my goal is to help honor its great past while also shepherding it to a brighter future."

Watt, who is married to former United States soccer star Kealia Ohai, spent two years with the club creating the design. He studied past kits and decided he wanted to bring back one of the club's old crests, an intricate shield that has symmetrical lions, roses, a bee and a knight's helmet. It was used from 1979 to 1983 and again from 1987 to 2009. There is also a subtle geometric pattern throughout the kit inspired by the stonework at Burnley's historic training facility, Gawthorpe Hall.

"I am merely a steward for this club," Watt said in the club's behind-the-scenes video of the making of the kit, "but the opportunity to create a kit with this badge and this crest and hopefully with the proper respect for what it means is an incredible honor for me and I hope everybody likes it."

"It's been great fun working with JJ on this project," Ed Stewart-Lockhart, Burnley's Chief Marketing Officer added, calling the jersey "future-retro." "He's brought incredible energy all the way through. You can see how much he's enjoyed it, but also how much it matters to him that we've got it right."

The club said that the first 100 fans to buy the jersey at their official store would get a collector's box that had an exclusive cap and signed photo of Watt. The first 100 online customers would also get an autographed photo.

Burnley will play in the EFL Championship this upcoming season. They were relegated after spending one year in the Premier League.

The cream kit will make its debut on Sunday, August 2 in a home friendly against Torino.

Watt continues to be involved in American football, too. He will serve as CBS Sports' lead NFL analyst while Tony Romo is on leave.

title: Jack Campbell Reveals Detroit Lions’ Massive Training Camp Goal
description: Jack Campbell delivered a clear message about Detroit’s defensive expectations. The Lions want to become the NFL’s most conditioned team, eliminate excuses against the run and create more turnovers.
fullText:
Jack Campbell is ready for the pads.

More than that, the Detroit Lions linebacker is ready for the part of training camp where conditioning, accountability, and physical football stop being talking points and start showing up on the field.

“Whenever the pads come on, they come on,” Campbell said. “It definitely makes things a little easier for me specifically. I’m excited. We have a great group of guys this year, and I’m excited to get into the thick of it and start colliding bodies.”

That sounds exactly like Campbell. No theatrics. No hesitation. Just a linebacker waiting for football to feel like football again.

Detroit’s preparation for Week 1 is already underway, and Campbell has set an ambitious standard for the roster.

“The process has already started,” Campbell said. “We’re getting ready for Week 1, and, in my opinion, we want to be the most conditioned team in the NFL. That’s what I think it takes.”

Conditioning rarely receives much attention once the regular season begins. It becomes impossible to ignore when a defense begins fading during a fourth-quarter drive.

Campbell does not want that happening to Detroit.

The Lions want to play fast, pursue the football and remain physical deep into games. That requires more than lifting weights or running sprints during the offseason.

“You’re definitely getting into football shape right now,” Campbell said. “For me, it’s difficult to practice football during the offseason because football is one explosive movement after another. You can sprint in a straight line during the offseason, but when you get out here, a lot of it is lateral, then vertical, then lateral and then vertical again. You can’t truly practice that.”

Training camp gives players the movement patterns, mental stress and repeated collisions that ordinary workouts cannot duplicate.

“This acclimation period is good for getting the body flowing again, getting the mind going and getting back into camp,” Campbell said. “You also start learning how different guys play. You begin recognizing that one guy is going to do one thing while another guy will react differently.”

Campbell’s strongest comments came while discussing Detroit’s run defense.

“I hang my hat on the run game, so hopefully there won’t be an issue there,” Campbell said. “There are no excuses. That’s not something we’re going to accept this year.”

That is a serious standard from the player expected to operate near the center of Detroit’s defense.

Stopping the run demands discipline across the entire front. One defender loses his gap, another gets caught out of position and suddenly a short gain becomes an explosive play.

Campbell does not care where a player sits on the depth chart.

“You have to get your job done. If you don’t do your job, it shows up blatantly on the tape. It doesn’t matter whether you’re the top player or the bottom player on the roster. We need you to do your job. Everybody will be held accountable.”

Campbell also placed himself first in that line of accountability.

“That accountability starts with me. I can continue improving in that area.”

That is the leadership Detroit needs from him. Campbell is no longer a young linebacker trying to find his footing. He is becoming one of the central voices of the defense.

Campbell is also using camp to sharpen a specific skill: forcing fumbles.

“Right now, I’m trying to continue developing my punch-outs. This is a good time to work on that.”

The challenge is creating the turnover without losing control of the tackle.

“In a live game, it takes a special talent to punch the football out while also securing the tackle. It’s very impressive. You have to consider the angle of the running back, where the sideline is, where your teammates are and how protected you are.”

Campbell admitted he has not produced the result he wants yet.

“Right now, I’m working on punching the ball out.I haven’t gotten one yet, so I need to be better.”

He pointed to Fred Warner’s forced fumble against Minnesota as an example of the technique he wants to master.

“The one time I saw it done was Fred Warner’s play against the Vikings at the goal line. He came in, squared the player up and got the ball out. Even if he had missed the football, I think he still would have made the tackle.”

That final detail matters. The takeaway attempt cannot come at the expense of the defense.

Campbell understands that talking about takeaways means very little without producing them.

“A lot of people talk about punching the ball out, but you have to apply it. Sometimes people overlook it, and then the opportunities aren’t there. Turnovers win games in the NFL.”

Detroit’s defense needs more game-changing plays, especially in tight divisional matchups where one possession can decide everything.

Campbell wants to become part of that solution.

“That’s something I want to do. I want to help in any way I can and be as productive as possible.”

An improved ability to force fumbles would add another layer to his game. Campbell already brings size, range and physicality. Creating turnovers would move him closer to becoming the complete linebacker Detroit envisioned when it drafted him.

Campbell said Detroit’s defensive identity still begins with Dan Campbell and defensive coordinator Kelvin Sheppard.

“Shep is still the same, and it starts with Dan. The feeling of the team starts with the entire team, and it feels identical. Everybody is hungry and ready to work.”

He also rejected the idea that the Lions are spending camp dwelling on last season.

“There’s all this talk about last year, but it’s a new year. Nobody is thinking about last year. Every season, you have to enter with the right mindset. If you don’t, it’s going to be a long year.”

Detroit can learn from the disappointment without allowing it to control the next season.

Campbell wants every player operating at full capacity, regardless of injuries or changes to the lineup.

“I’m looking for everybody, including myself, to push things to the maximum and lay everything on the line every week. No matter who gets hurt, whoever is put into the game is expected to play at a high level.”

Not just from the stars. From everyone.

Jack Campbell’s message was direct.

The Lions want to become the NFL’s most conditioned team. They will not tolerate excuses against the run. Every player will be accountable, and every defender must be prepared to perform when called upon.

Campbell is also challenging himself to create more turnovers and become a more productive centerpiece of Detroit’s defense.

Now the Lions get to find out who can live up to the standard.

fullText:
MILWAUKEE (AP) — CBS NFL analyst and former Dallas Cowboys quarterback Tony Romo had an open container of alcohol in his vehicle when he was stopped by police last week and later arrested on suspicion of driving under the influence, authorities said.

According to one of three citations released by the Milwaukee County Sheriff’s Office, the “open bottle of an alcoholic beverage” was discovered in the passenger’s side of Romo’s black Jeep during an inventory before it was towed.

Another citation said police stopped Romo on Interstate 43 on July 23 after he was seen passing cars in a gore area, which separates interstate traffic from cars entering from an on-ramp. Police said Romo questioned what a gore area was during the stop.

Romo performed poorly on field sobriety tests and was taken into custody, booked and released. Court records show Romo was later cited for refusing “to take test for intoxication after arrest.” He has a court appearance scheduled for Sept. 21.

According to body camera footage released earlier this week, Romo told deputies he had been coming from a golf course and was on his way “to visit grandma and grandpa” when he was stopped.

A deputy told Romo he suspected him of being impaired because he had “red glassy eyes” and an “odor of an intoxicating alcoholic beverage.”

Romo went to high school about 35 miles from Milwaukee in Burlington, Wisconsin.

The 46-year-old Romo has been the lead game analyst for CBS’ NFL coverage since 2017 after making four Pro Bowl appearances during an NFL career that ran from 2004-16 and was spent entirely with Dallas.

Romo remains the Cowboys’ franchise leader in career touchdown passes with 248. He held the franchise record for career passing yards (34,183) until Dak Prescott overtook him last season.

He subsequently joined the Las Vegas Raiders and rushed for 420 yards and four touchdowns in 2024. His 3.2 yards per carry reflected the difficulty he had producing consistently in a struggling offense, although he added 36 receptions for 294 yards and another touchdown.

Miami signed Mattison in 2025 with the expectation that he could provide a more physical complement to DeâVon Achane. That opportunity disappeared when the neck injury ended his season before it began.

Houston now represents a possible route back.

Jonathan Taylor drops major hint about his next Colts contract originally appeared on The Sporting News. Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here.

Three years after a contract dispute dominated headlines in Indianapolis, Jonathan Taylor is entering training camp with a much different mindset.

In 2023, Taylor’s search for a new contract became one of the NFL’s biggest offseason storylines. The star running back staged a hold-in, requested a trade following a widely publicized meeting with late Colts owner Jim Irsay, and faced an uncertain future with the franchise.

title: The phone call that made Briton an NFL trailblazer
description: Seydou Traore is the first graduate of the UK-based NFL Academy to be drafted in the NFL. This is how he beat the odds.
fullText:
Seydou Traore has been waiting four hours for the phone call that will change his life. When it comes, he is the picture of calm. Next to him, his mum Zaia is anything but.

Traore and his family are sitting backstage at the NFL Draft, where the 23-year-old Briton - who did not see his loved ones for five years after moving to the US to try to become an NFL player - has just been told his dream is coming true.

Zaia, who is French-Algerian, lets out a 'zaghrouta' - a celebratory trilling sound that is traditional in north Africa - sheds tears of joy and has an out-of-body experience in a reaction that goes viral.

"I was in a trance," she tells BBC Sport. "I was like 'oh my God, it's happening, he's done it'. That's what I kept telling myself. It was pride and relief because it's been years, and it was all worth it."

Of all the social media content around Seydou's achievement in being the first graduate of England's NFL Academy to complete his pathway to the NFL, it is the clip of his mum he keeps watching.

He knows that she knows exactly what it has taken to defy the odds and become an NFL trailblazer.

A pep talk from the great Travis Kelce was just a tiny part.

Born and raised in south London, Traore was naturally athletic and tried many sports. He was playing football as a goalkeeper when he found American football at 16 with London Warriors.

In 2019 he earned a place in the first intake at the NFL Academy, a development programme initially based in north London and now in Loughborough. The academy recruits from many sport backgrounds and American football experience is not necessary.

Almost all draft prospects come through the American college system, which is why the academy was designed to help international players earn scholarships and prepare them for the NFL, mentally and physically.

Each year about one million teenagers play American football at high school in the US. About 0.08% of them reach the NFL.

One can therefore imagine how the odds are stacked against an international player like Traore.

But he applied himself to his dream, getting up at 5am and working all day every day to get better, either at the academy or training.

And the following summer, he had a breakthrough.

Traore's mum was in the kitchen when he came in and told her: "Some Americans want to speak with you. I've been talking to them for a while and, basically, I'm going to America."

Unknown to Zaia, her son had secured a spot at Florida high school Clearwater Academy. She told him: "I can't afford to come and see you, you'll be there by yourself."

For Traore's sister Zeinab, four years his senior, the thought of him moving 4,500 miles from home was even more difficult.

"He's like my first child so I'm protective," she says. "I was concerned at first. I thought it was too big a jump because he was still young."

Traore had been laying the foundations for this move for some time, making videos to showcase his skills.

One of them found its way to Clearwater head coach Jesse Chinchar.

"Wow, who's that?" Chinchar wondered as he watched a 6ft 3in guy leaping in the air to make a one-handed catch.

Little did he know that he was watching a Londoner who was yet to play a full-sided game of American football. But Clearwater had a track record of recruiting international players and helping them earn college scholarships.

"I did a bit more digging but there was no game film, just clips of him doing athletic stuff," says Chinchar.

"We got talking to Seydou and it felt like he was going to compete and wanted it for all the right reasons. You could tell how much it meant to him.

"It was kind of a wild adventure because he was one of the most raw, unknown commodities we had brought in, but we thought 'if this kid comes over and it works out, this could change his life'."

From day one Chinchar thought "we got something".

Traore learned his first playbook in a matter of days, which is like learning a new language. And playing as a wide receiver, he was immediately dominant against kids who had played the game their whole life.

He thinks his goalkeeping skills helped.

"Hand-eye coordination, tracking and locating balls, leaping down low or up high, and attacking the ball at corner kicks, that translates very well," Traore says.

"That's how American football is when they throw the ball up to you, you attack it at its highest point."

Chinchar agrees, adding: "I've felt that my guys who had a background in soccer have that understanding of spatial awareness, which I think in [American] football is an under-rated trait."

Chinchar was also impressed by Traore's character and self-belief. Even when he received his first college offer, he bet on himself getting a better one. That eventually came from Arkansas State.

Their head coach Butch Jones was working late when his tight ends coach came into his office and said: "I keep hearing about this player. I think he's special, there's something different about him."

They watched videos of Traore and Jones soon made a "hefty comparison". He called Seydou a clone of Travis Kelce, whom he coached at Cincinnati and helped convert into one of the best tight ends in NFL history.

"Seydou's size and stature coupled with his athleticism - the way he ran, the way he caught the ball – it made him a rare commodity," says Jones. "He had unlimited potential."

Traore had barely played at tight end and had already committed to another college. Jones therefore had to 'flip' him - so he called on his old friend.

He set up a group video call in which Kelce gave Seydou some advice and convinced him to trust coach Jones and his staff. Seydou signed in February 2021 and transitioned to tight end, showing natural instincts for the position.

Traore saw himself as a "big ball of clay" that Jones could mould, and the coach says he was "like a sponge" in terms of retaining information.

"In his first year Seydou looked like a young deer that could run but hadn't really matured yet, grown into his body," adds Jones.

"By year two you could see that development. He made some plays where you were in awe on the sideline."

Like Kelce, Traore can hurdle defenders, and in 2022 he was named the best tight end in the Sun Belt Conference. But he was determined to step up to the top level of college football and play in one of the Power Four conferences.

Seydou spent early 2023 with Colorado, whose tight ends coach called him out during a news conference, questioning his "toughness" and work ethic.

"We talked a few times when he was at Colorado, going through some tough times," says Jones.

"There was a lot of adversity through his journey, but he never gave up. He had that mental disposition it takes, every single day, to fight off the doubt that can creep in, especially when you're away from home."

In those moments, Seydou thought about his family.

"Knowing what I'd left and what I was trying to become was very motivating," he says.

After a term at Colorado, Seydou felt it best for his development to move on and he went to Mississippi State, who play in college football's most prestigious conference, the Southeastern.

But because he had transferred twice in quick succession, NCAA rules meant he could not play during 2023. All he could do was train.

It was then that Seydou found out just how much he wanted it. He treated it as a chance to improve his game, and when he finally played for Mississippi State in 2024, he was one of their top receiving threats.

Then in 2025, he began to catch the eye of NFL scouts. He scored a career-high five touchdowns and became a fans' favourite for his new tea-sipping celebration, a nod to the British stereotype.

Seydou's family also visited twice, seeing him for the first time in five years and witnessing just how "crazy" American college sport is.

There was a military flyover, fireworks and a cacophony of cowbells among the 60,000 crowd - a long-held tradition at Mississippi State.

With Seydou's college career now complete, it was time to enter the NFL Draft.

NFL teams recruit their best players through the draft, a three-day process that has become one of the biggest events in the NFL calendar.

Each year about 260 players are selected across seven rounds. They get a call from their new team and a few minutes later their name is announced on stage. A record 805,000 fans attended this year's draft in Pittsburgh.

Hundreds of prospects are evaluated by NFL experts and Seydou was projected to be picked on the final day, when rounds four to seven take place.

Former player Efe Obada was there to support the international hopefuls. Having also gone from London Warriors to the NFL, he is an academy ambassador and saw Traore at the try-outs in 2019.

So after the Miami Dolphins called Traore late in the fifth round, Obada "kind of hijacked" his announcement.

He ran into the office NFL commissioner Roger Goodell was using and told him "I wanna do it". Goodell agreed it "made sense" and they went on stage together to welcome Traore into the NFL.

"I thought it would be symbolic, passing on the torch," says Obada. "I've kind of gone through that journey and I wanted people to know that it's a moment. [Being drafted] doesn't just happen. This sport is about endurance and commitment."

As a former London Warriors coach, Aden Durde was aware of Traore's talent before he too attended the first academy try-outs.

And the British defensive co-ordinator, who helped the Seattle Seahawks win the Super Bowl in February, smiled when he heard Traore's name mentioned during this year's pre-draft process.

"It's so cool to see him go to different colleges and really kick down the door and break barriers," he says.

"That was the vision of the NFL Academy all those years ago. He's the first one and there's going to be plenty more. It's exciting times."

Travis Clayton was the first ex-academy player to be drafted but only spent a brief period with the programme in 2019 and did not attend a US college, so Traore is the first of its alumni to follow the full pathway.

Since the academy's inception more than 75 students have secured college football scholarships in the US.

Traore has remained cool, calm and collected throughout his journey, even when he strode on to the NFL Draft stage. Draped in a British flag, he stopped to put on a Dolphins cap and do his tea-sipping celebration for the camera.

But one day in June, far from the draft spotlight, his excitement got the better of him.

Zeinab says they used to joke about who would be the first to buy their mum a house. Seydou knew he had won when he signed a four-year rookie contract worth $4.8m (£3.6m).

And it was his older sister, not his mum, whom he called to say "I'm signing right now!"

Not all drafted players are guaranteed to play from the start of their rookie season. Teams must whittle their roster from 90 or 91 players down to 53 by 31 August.

Traore is trying to earn a spot during Miami's training camp but is backing himself to continue his remarkable journey in the NFL.

"It feels good [to be here]," he adds. "But I keep telling everyone, it's just the beginning."

title: EA Sports reveal Madden '27 player ratings. Where do the 49ers rank?
description: Check out the San Francisco 49ers player ratings on EA Sports' Madden NFL 27. See which players were given a 99 rating and who weren't.
fullText:
The release of EA Sports' Madden NFL 27 means that we're that much closer to football season. The video game will be made available Aug. 13 with pre-orders are available and early access on Aug. 6 and 10.

EA Sports released its player ratings Wednesday and this is where the football world really gets to chirping. It's where the talks of bragging rights for who's the best player really get brewing between the athletes and fans alike.

Six players had a 99 rating, but none of them were members of the San Francisco 49ers. Instead the 49ers' division rivals, the Los Angeles Rams, had a couple players atop the list as quarterback Matthew Stafford and newly acquired edge rusher Myles Garrett were given 99 ratings. The other signal caller in the league to be rated 99 is Buffalo Bills' Josh Allen.

Making the 99 list was Seattle Seahawks wide receiver Jaxon Smith-Njigba. He is the top-rated receiver in NFC, according to Madden NFL 27. Cincinnati Bengals receiver Jamarr Chase is only other wideout with a 99 rating.

Madden NFL 27 says that Arizona Cardinals tight end Trey McBride is the best at his position, giving him a 99 rating.

Although there weren't any 49ers players rated 99, they still have some of the best players in the league, according to their Madden ratings. Here's a look at the San Francisco 49ers player ratings and leading attributes.

The 49ers might not have a player with a 99 preseason rating, but some are pretty close. A good start to the season and they could progress to a 99 easily.

San Francisco running back Christian McCaffrey has a 97 rating. Some of his attribute ratings include a 90 speed, 93 agility and 99 awareness. He's rated the second-best tailback in the league behind the Detroit Lions' 98-rated Jahmyr Gibbs.

McBride is considered the best tight end in the league, but don't forget about George Kittle. Although coming off of a torn right Achilles, Kittle is still considered the second-best tight end in football with a 96 rating. Kittle has a 77 run block rating and a 78 impact blocking rating. He possesses some of the best hands with a 94 catching, 89 spectacular catch and 89 catch in traffic ratings.

Trent Williams is still considered one of the best at his position. The left tackle has a 96 rating. He's tied with Denver Broncos' Garett Bolles, and both are a couple ratings behind Detroit Lions' Penei Sewell, who has a 98 rating.

Veteran wide receiver Mike Evans is still given his props. Madden NFL 27 gave Evans a 91 rating with attributes including 97 jumping, 97 catch in traffic, 96 spectacular catch and 93 catching.

A player rating for 49ers quarterback Brock Purdy was not yet available on the EA Sports website.

49ers linebacker Fred Warner did not have a player rating available on the EA Sports website.

title: Jalen Carter signs record $152m extension with Eagles
description: Jalen Carter has signed a four-year extension with the Philadelphia Eagles, the club said Tuesday, in a deal that reportedly makes him the highest-paid defensive tackle in NFL history.Carter has 13.5 quarterback sacks and 108 tackles across his first three seasons with Philadelphia.
fullText:
Jalen Carter has signed a four-year extension with the Philadelphia Eagles, the club said Tuesday, in a deal that reportedly makes him the highest-paid defensive tackle in NFL history.

Though the 2025 Super Bowl winners did not disclose financial terms, US media said the extension was worth $152 million (133.5 million euros), or $38 million per year, with $106 million guaranteed.

Carter, 25, is one of the NFL's most highly-rated young defenders, having been selected to each of the last two Pro Bowls.

He was drafted ninth in the first round in 2023, and became a cornerstone of the Eagles' vaunted defense.

Carter has 13.5 quarterback sacks and 108 tackles across his first three seasons with Philadelphia.

His initial four-year deal had already been extended by one year, but the new contract locks down his long-term future.

"He disrupts the game, he's smart, and he plays hard," Eagles defensive coordinator Vic Fangio said in a statement.

"There aren't many like him out there and I'm glad he's on our side."

The talented star has also drawn controversy.

Carter was ejected from last year's NFL season-opener before playing a snap for spitting on Dallas Cowboys quarterback Dak Prescott.

Just weeks before his 2023 draft, Carter was charged with reckless driving and racing, after a University of Georgia teammate and staff member in a different vehicle were killed in a late-night street race.

Carter, who was not under the influence of alcohol or drugs, pleaded no contest to two misdemeanor charges and did not receive jail time.

title: How the Jets have built a better defense than the NFL realizes
description: Breaking down the improvements in the Jets defense ahead of the 2026 NFL season.
fullText:
The New York Jets have understandably received attention for the changes they've made on offense during the 2026 NFL offseason, but their most impressive work may have come on the other side of the football.

General manager Darren Mougey and head coach Aaron Glenn didn't simply add recognizable names. They built a defense with a clear philosophy in mind.

Every level of the unit now features a blend of proven veterans, ascending young players, and developmental prospects capable of competing for meaningful roles. It's a strategy that has largely flown under the radar. The Jets attacked the defensive front with both proven production and developmental upside.

Veterans such as David Onyemata, T'Vondre Sweat, Kingsley Enagbare, and Joseph Ossai give New York additional experience, physicality, and pass-rushing versatility. Their arrivals should lessen the burden on returning starters while creating healthy competition throughout training camp.

The front office also invested in the future through the 2026 draft. Rookie edge rusher David Bailey brings intriguing pass-rush potential, while defensive tackle Darrell Jackson Jr. adds another young body capable of developing along the interior defensive line. The second level received similar attention.

Linebacker Demario Davis gives the Jets one of the league's most respected defensive leaders, while undrafted rookies Jaden Keller, Chase Wilson, and Nathan Voorhis provide developmental depth that will compete for roster spots and special teams responsibilities throughout the summer. The secondary may be where the transformation is most noticeable.

Acquiring Minkah Fitzpatrick immediately changes the complexion of the defense. His experience, versatility, and playmaking ability provide Glenn with another proven veteran capable of impacting games in multiple ways. Cornerback Nahshon Wright adds size and depth, while rookie D'Angelo Ponds injects youth and athleticism into an already competitive defensive backfield. Rookie safety VJ Payne further strengthens the group's long-term outlook.

One of the most overlooked aspects of New York's offseason is that these additions weren't made simply to fill vacancies. They were made to create competition. Successful defenses rarely rely on 11 starters alone. They survive injuries, adapt to weekly matchups, and sustain production because quality depth exists behind the first team.

The Jets appear to understand that reality.

Instead of chasing splash signings at one position, they distributed resources across the entire defense.

That's exactly the type of roster construction Glenn has emphasized throughout his coaching career.

title: The Most Important Packers: No. 1 — QB Jordan Love
description: Green Bay's Jordan Love has become one of the NFL's top quarterbacks, but is just 1-3 in the postseason.
fullText:
The Green Bay Packers were arguably the most disappointing team in football last year. And perhaps no one did less with more than Packers’ coach Matt LaFleur.

Green Bay headed into the 2025 season with one of the NFL’s top rosters, then traded for star defensive end Micah Parsons 10 days before the year began. Suddenly, Packer Nation was dreaming of their first Super Bowl appearance since 2010.

Instead, Green Bay went a remarkably unsatisfying 9-8-1 overall and was the NFC’s No. 7 seed for a third consecutive year. The Packers then blew a 21-3 halftime lead in the Wild Card round against Chicago, gave up 25 fourth quarter points and eventually suffered a shocking 31-27 loss to the arch-rival Bears.

“No way you should lose games in this league when you’re up that much,” running back Josh Jacobs said.

Green Bay, which began the year 9-3-1, finished the season with five straight losses. The Packers now enter 2026 with the league’s fourth-longest losing streak.

Collapsing late in games was the story of Green Bay’s 2025 campaign.

Green Bay had double digit leads in the final minutes twice against Chicago and also vs. Cleveland and somehow went 0-3 in those games. The Packers’ odds of losing all three contests were 1-in-250,000, yet they somehow did it.

“That (expletive), it’s starting to get damn-near embarrassing,” safety Javon Bullard said.

Rebounding won’t be easy as the Packers were hit hard in free agency and didn't have a first round draft pick.

Green Bay’s first training camp practice is July 29. Between now and then I will count down the ‘30 Most Important Packers’ heading into the 2026 campaign.

For the fourth straight year, quarterback Jordan Love is No. 1.

Love had arguably his finest season yet in 2025.

Love had a career-best passer rating of 101.2 that ranked No. 6 in the NFL. Love completed 291 of 439 passes (66.3%) for 3,381 yards and 23 touchdowns vs. just six interceptions.

Love’s interception percentage was just 1.4% and his touchdown-to-interception ratio was 3.83-1.

Love finished eighth in the league in yards per attempt (7.70) and tied for eighth in explosive passes (16-plus yards) with 81.

When teams blitzed Love, it usually backfired as he posted a 109.5 passer rating against the blitz that ranked fifth in the league.

And while the Packers’ playoff loss to Chicago is one of the more forgettable nights in team history, Love did all he could to lead Green Bay to victory. Love threw four touchdowns, no interceptions and posted a 103.8 passer rating that night in Chicago.

Love, a controversial first round draft pick in 2020, sat for three years behind Hall of Famer Aaron Rodgers. Then, when Love got his chance to take over in 2023, he made the most of it.

From 2023-25, Love ranks sixth in the league with 80 touchdowns. He’s also No. 8 in passing yards (10,929) and yards per attempt (7.57).

Love made all 19 starts in 2023, threw 37 touchdown passes and just 13 interceptions. During a two-month window between Week 11 and Green Bay’s NFC divisional playoff game at San Francisco, Love threw a remarkable 23 touchdowns and just one interception.

That’s something Green Bay legends Bart Starr, Brett Favre and Aaron Rodgers never did.

Love completed 409 of 634 passes (64.5%) for 4,625 yards and finished with a 98.5 passer rating in 2023. Love ranked second in the league in TD passes and seventh in total passing yards (4,159) that season.

Love signed a four-year, $220 million contract during training camp in 2024, then had an up and down second season as Green Bay’s starter.

Love suffered a sprained medial collateral ligament in the Packers’ Week 1 loss to Philadelphia and missed the next two games. He later missed half of a Week 8 game at Jacksonville with a groin injury and three quarters of a Week 18 loss to Chicago with a right elbow injury.

Despite those injuries, Love threw 25 TDs, 11 interceptions and had a 96.7 passer rating. Love ranked 19th in the league passing yards (3,389) and completed 63.1% of his passes.

Love had a passer rating of at least 107.7 in five straight games between Weeks 11-15, but was at 92.0, or less, the last four contests.

Love then threw three interceptions in Green Bay’s loss to Philadelphia in the NFC Wild Card game and had a season-low passer rating of 41.5.

When the season ended, many suggested Love had regressed in his second season as a starter.

“I mean, what is a step back is what I’d ask?” Love said when asked if he regressed in 2024. “Everybody has different opinions, things like that. You got to block that stuff out.”

Love, who will turn 28 in November, has done his part in carrying on the tremendous quarterback tradition in Green Bay.

He can make every throw. He’s as cool as January night in Green Bay. He’s become more of a vocal leader and he’s highly regarded by his teammates.

Now, the No. 1 question around Love is can he take the Packers on a deep playoff run?

Love won his first playoff game in 2023, but has lost his last three.

Fair or not, players are judged by what they do in the postseason.

There are 35 quarterbacks that have won a Super Bowl. Fifteen are in the Hall of Fame and eight others are locks or likely entrees when they become eligible (Tom Brady, Patrick Mahomes, Drew Brees, Ben Roethlisberger, Aaron Rodgers, Matthew Stafford, Eli Manning and Russell Wilson).

Love has all the tools to become one of the NFL’s elite quarterbacks, but needs to lead Green Bay deep into the playoffs for that narrative to develop.

“Jordan's been awesome, man. Like every year, he just continues to grow as a leader, you know. His consistency is remarkable. Who he is on a daily basis, showing up, how he works, how he leads others, he's pulling guys with them. So I'm really excited about what, you know, is in store for him.” — Packers coach Matt LaFleur on Love

“When I stepped away, it was just two seasons with him, right, so a pretty big difference in maturity, of the command of the offense and also, so it was a quite a few years difference there. But it was just a lot of fun when I step back in it and got to see him really running the show and him in complete control and the comfortability. I think one of his best traits is just that his cool, calm, collected mentality, and then just seeing that match with all the high-level functionality of the mental part of the game. It was really cool to see that when I got back – just a natural growth for his game.” — Packers quarterbacks coach Luke Getsy on Love

“For me, my biggest thing that I’ve noticed since I got back is just my feet in the pocket, trying to be as smooth and consistent as possible. When I go through my reads, get into my hitches and not getting antsy, not getting to that point where you’re trying to move through the pocket too fast. Just staying calm, staying relaxed, move through my reads.” — Love on what he focused on this offseason
