title: Falcons land WR help in 2027 NFL mock draft from CBS Sports
description: Falcons take 6-foot-3 Texas WR in 2027 NFL mock draft from CBS Sports
fullText:
There are some major question marks surrounding the Atlanta Falcons' roster as the team prepares to kick off training camp this week in Flowery Branch. From the starting quarterback competition to the battle for the No. 2 wide receiver job, Falcons head coach Kevin Stefanski has much to figure out over the next month.

The team signed former first-round pick Jahan Dotson to replace speedster Darnell Mooney, but it's fair to question whether or not he's capable of filling that role. Dotson's career stats suggest otherwise, however, it's tough to produce when you're stuck behind two elite receivers, as he was in Philadelphia.

Former Georgia wide receiver Zachariah Branch appears to have a bright future, assuming his effectiveness isn't hindered by his lack of size. Depending on how this season goes, the Falcons may or may not be looking for a new No. 2 wide receiver in 2027.

Atlanta lands a perfect complement to Drake London in a new CBS Sports mock draft from Mike Renner. The Falcons were projected to take Texas wide receiver Cam Coleman with the sixth overall pick in the 2027 NFL Draft.

"Cam Coleman is a wildly explosive 6-foot-3, 200-pound wideout who spent the past two seasons stuck with poor quarterback play at Auburn," wrote Renner. "That changes this year as he heads to Texas to pair with Arch Manning. He should be a household name by season's end."

Coleman racked up 93 receptions for 1,306 receiving yards and 13 touchdowns (14.0 yards per catch) over the last two seasons at Auburn. The Falcons have dealt with similar quarterback issues over the past few years, so Coleman would feel right at home in Atlanta.

The Falcons did re-sign London to a four-year, $141 million contract extension during the offseason, however, there is still a clear lack of depth behind him. Branch could be a long-term option in the slot with No. 2 upside, but it wouldn't hurt to add to the receiver room in 2027.

For now, Atlanta is set to kick off training camp with its current wide receiver group. Although, we wouldn't be surprised to see the team add someone like Stefon Diggs or Keenan Allen before camp ends.

title: Chiefs’ training camp video of Patrick Mahomes and QB room goes viral

The Kansas City Chiefs posted a video of Patrick Mahomes and the QB room throwing passes during training camp. It featured the two-time NFL MVP, along with Justin Fields, Garrett Nussmeier and Chris Oladokun.

Mahomes will reportedly be ready to return as early as Week 1. He has 53 career NFL starts under his belt and will likely be the team’s QB2 once the three-time Super Bowl champion is back to full strength.

The Pittsburgh Steelers waived Oladokun in 2022, but he signed a practice squad deal with Kansas City. The team promoted him to the active roster on Dec. 20 following Mahomes’ injury the week prior, and he started his first NFL game on Christmas Day against the Denver Broncos.

The Chiefs will likely ease Mahomes back before he takes over his QB1 job full-time. Fields will serve as his backup, while Nussmeier and Oladokun will battle for the third-string role.

title: Nathaniel Hackett's "definitely a rookie" remark about Jeremiyah Love is getting overblown
description: We're in the business of finding and sharing and analyzing interesting remarks from anyone in the NFL ecosystem.
fullText:
We're in the business of finding and sharing and analyzing interesting remarks from anyone in the NFL ecosystem. But certain supposedly controversial comments aren't really as big of a deal as some may interpret them to be.

Case in point: Cardinals offensive coordinator Nathaniel Hackett is catching some heat for comments he made on Saturday about rookie running back Jeremiyah Love.

"He's definitely a rookie, and — as we've talked about," Hackett said. "And he'll keep growing every single day. I'm very excited for him. All those guys. Not just him."

The broader context has to be considered, especially since Hackett specifically added "as we've talked about."

Earlier in the session, Hackett addressed the challenges that first-year players face when training camp opens. The question related to the things that are different for rookies.

"Everything you can imagine," Hackett said. "I mean, coming to this league is — I mean, just the speed is so different. You talk about the speed, being in a new building. . . . [I]t's a whole new environment. New people to work with, and definitely new playbooks that are very, very intricate. Due to the fact of all the things that we see and all the different — I mean, just our defense out there. I mean, you get almost everything and more. Which is great, because it helps you for the season, but for a young player to have to be able to adjust and learn just basic system and then apply it to different defenses. It takes some time. So heads are spinning right now, especially after two days, but I think it'll just get better and better. That's the goal."

Hackett wasn't dismissing or minimizing Love. He's a rookie. Like the rest of the rookies. Everything is different. Everything is new. "Heads are spinning," as Hackett said.

Training camp is the time to slow, and eventually to stop, the spinning. They have plenty of time to get Love ready to go. For now, after only two days, he's beginning the adjustment.

That's all it means. Which makes the comment not nearly as alarming as some are making it out to be.
